title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: species/number unity fail; Porphyry; proposition unclear
pass_a_gloss: In what way are all 'one man in Adam'? By Porphyry's specific unity—many becoming one by sharing the species? That does nothing for charging Adam's actual sin to everyone, because deeds belong to concrete individuals, not to a genus or species; and once proper differences are granted, nobody is Adam more than any other man, Adam being under the human species like the rest. Or were they viewed as numerically one individual in Adam? No fiction could be falser. So what do you intend by the proposition? I admit I cannot see a non-absurd sense for it.
pass_b_english: For how are all men considered as one man in Adam? As Porphyry said—by participation of the species many men are one, that is, by specific unity? But that cannot help the imputation of Adam's actual sin to all men: for actions belong to individuals (supposits), not to genus or species; and when the proper differences by which they are distinguished among themselves are set down, all men are no more Adam than any other man whatever is: for Adam is contained under the species of man no less than the remaining individual men. Or do you mean that all men were considered as one man numerically in Adam? Nothing falser could be feigned than that consideration. What, then, do you mean by this proposition? I frankly confess I do not understand what sense not foolish it can have.
source_text: Nam quomodo omnes homines considerantur tanquam unus homo in Adamo? an quomodo dixit Porphyrius participatione speciei multos homines esse unum, unitate scilicet specifica? at id juvare non potest imputationem peccati actualis Adami omnibus hominibus: actiones enim sunt suppositorum, non autem generis, aut speciei: nec positis, quibus inter se distinguuntur, differentiis propriis omnes homines magis sunt Adamus, quam alius quilibet homo: continetur enim sub hominis specie Adamus haud secus quam reliqui individui homines. An vis omnes homines consideratos fuisse tanquam unum numero hominem in Adamo? nihil fingi posset falsius ista consideratione. Quid igitur tibi vis hac propositione? Ea, fateor ingenue, non intelligo quem sensum non ineptum habere possit.

choices.choice: Reject species and numeric unity as grounds for actual-sin imputation
